items.title: Joe Mares Jr. Interview, 1960-04-08
items.q: Alma Schobert was the only fellow could read in the band

ctx.x: I know when I first met George Brunus, 1936 in New York, I gave him a couple of those Jeanette records, and he said that Farewell Blues is something that Rap worked that out of the weary blues. He took a little phrase out of the weary blues.

Well, it has that Shake It and Break It deal in there. And a lot of them record a lot of their own tunes, the Bugle called Rag and things like that. They were made up, and they lost a lot of tunes. For instance, Alma Schobert was the only fellow could read in the band, and what I hear, he copied a lot of things that later on he used, like Nobody's Sweetheart, Copenhagen, and I know for a fact that Paul wrote the tune called, I Never Knew What A Gal Could Do. Alma Schobert gets credit for it, but I'm sure Paul…

items.title: Joe Mares Jr. Interview, 1960-04-08
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I met Paul's wife. She was the brother of some police captain or something? Yeah, her brother Tom was captain of police [INTERVIEWEE] in the first district of Chicago.

ctx.x: Well, I mentioned Jess Stacy was on piano. In fact, Paul recommended Jess Stacy to Benny Goodman. And that's where Jess went into Ben Goodman for Paul's recommendation. Of course, Benny Goodman is very good friends with Paul. In fact, Benny played for Paul's wedding when he was in short pants. Really? Yeah, Benny was only at that time 16 years old.
